skill.name: template-skill
skill.description: Minimal template for drafting a new Claude or Codex skill with frontmatter and an instruction section.
skill.summary: Provides a blank SKILL.md scaffold for authors starting a new AI skill.
skill.author: ComposioHQ

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found no executable code, network access, environment access, filesystem operations, or external commands. The only scanned file is SKILL.md with a placeholder skill template and no prompt injection indicators. No evidence found of malicious intent or data exfiltration.

content.value_statement: New skill authors need a clear starting structure before writing domain instructions. This template provides a minimal SKILL.md scaffold for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Provides minimal frontmatter for a skill name and description.
Marks where authors should add operating instructions.
Serves as a blank starting point for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skills.
Keeps the package prompt-only with no scripts or executable assets.
limitations: It does not include task-specific instructions or examples.
It does not provide scripts, tools, or automated checks.
It requires authors to replace the placeholder description before use.
It does not define a domain workflow or specialized behavior.

use_cases.title: Start a New Skill
use_cases.description: Use the scaffold when creating the first draft of a new AI skill.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Drafts
use_cases.description: Give contributors a shared structure for skill names, descriptions, and instructions.

use_cases.title: Review Template Structure
use_cases.description: Check that a submitted skill has basic frontmatter before deeper content review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this template to draft a skill for [task]. Replace the name, description, and instruction section with clear guidance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner authors need a first skill outline.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the Template for a Team
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this template into a shared team skill for [workflow]. Include ownership notes, scope, and expected user requests.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants consistent skill drafts.

prompt_templates.title: Add Operational Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this template with clear boundaries for [domain]. Include allowed actions, unsupported requests, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Marketplace Submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this template to prepare a publishable skill for [audience]. Replace placeholders and summarize capabilities, limits, and safe usage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced authors are preparing a marketplace entry.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks for a blank skill starting point.
output_examples.output: A minimal skill draft with a name, a description placeholder, and a clear area for instructions.

output_examples.input: A team wants a shared structure for future skills.
output_examples.output: A consistent outline that separates skill metadata from operational guidance.

output_examples.input: A reviewer checks whether the package contains executable behavior.
output_examples.output: The package is identified as prompt-only and limited to a short SKILL.md template.

best_practices: Replace all placeholders before publishing the skill.
Keep instructions specific, testable, and tied to the skill purpose.
Review the final skill for prompt injection text and unsupported claims.
anti_patterns: Publishing the template without replacing the placeholder description.
Adding hidden instructions that override user or system direction.
Claiming automated capabilities that the prompt-only template does not provide.

faq.question: Is this a complete skill?
faq.answer: No. It is a starter template that needs real instructions before use.

faq.question: Does it run code?
faq.answer: No. The audited package contains only SKILL.md and no executable files.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can I publish it unchanged?
faq.answer: You should not publish it unchanged because it still contains placeholders.

faq.question: Does it access user data?
faq.answer: No evidence found of data access, network use, or environment variable reads.

faq.question: How should authors customize it?
faq.answer: Replace the name, description, and instruction section with task-specific guidance.
